title: Reverse Linked List
statement:
You are given the head of a singly linked list. Reverse the list so that every link points the other way, and return the head of the reversed list.

The list is described by its values from head to tail. Print the values of the reversed list from its new head to its new tail.

Interviewers often ask for two versions of this problem: one that follows pointers iteratively and one that uses recursion (the call stack as the extra storage). Either is accepted here; a solution that relinks the existing nodes uses O(1) extra space.
input_format:
The first line contains an integer `n`, the number of nodes.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers, the node values from head to tail.
output_format: Print the `n` values of the reversed list, space-separated, on one line.

examples.explanation: The old tail (23) becomes the new head, and each node now points to the node that used to precede it.
A single node is its own reverse.
This list reads the same in both directions, so the output equals the input. The nodes are still relinked.

hints: While walking the list, you must remember where each node used to point before you overwrite its next link.
Keep three references: the previous node (initially null), the current node, and the node after the current one. At each step point `current.next` back at `previous`, then move all three forward.
The recursive version reverses the rest of the list first, then makes the node after the current one point back at the current node and clears the current node's own link.

import sys

def main():
    data = sys.stdin.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    vals = data[1:1 + n]
    prev = None
    # build the list as (value, next) pairs, then reverse it by relinking
    nxt = list(range(1, n)) + [-1]
    cur = 0
    prev = -1
    while cur != -1:
        after = nxt[cur]
        nxt[cur] = prev
        prev = cur
        cur = after
    out = []
    cur = prev
    while cur != -1:
        out.append(vals[cur])
        cur = nxt[cur]
    print(' '.join(out))

main()
